evidence.E1: Deliberate and structural, not incidental: acceptance path is app.py `_receive` (verify -> dedup -> commit -> return, src/webhookd/app.py:265-421) and processing is a separate `Worker` thread pool (src/webhookd/worker.py) fed by the store-as-queue with leases (store.py:368-414). The seam between them is one call, `on_accept=self.worker.notify` (app.py:535), and it can be turned off entirely with `[worker] enabled = false` to run `webhookd worker` as a separate tier. Measured effect: 2.2ms 202 against a 3-second handler.

unanticipated_findings: Dedup-key collision inside the `h:` namespace, contradicting the guarantee stated in the code comment. src/webhookd/app.py:119-121 uses the delivery-id header verbatim as `"h:" + header_value` when it is <=200 chars, but hashes it to `"h:sha256:" + sha256(value)` when it is longer. Those two forms share a namespace, so a sender can craft a short id that collides with the hashed form of a long one. Reproduced: `compute_delivery_key(sender, delivery_id_header_value="A"*201, ...)` and `compute_delivery_key(sender, delivery_id_header_value="sha256:" + sha256(b"A"*201).hexdigest(), ...)` both return `h:sha256:dea81b358bf5398fcac273cd724126e665c20d2ab58957a01beedd2df1f502f4` (printed `COLLIDE: True`). The second delivery is silently swallowed as a duplicate (200, no work queued, no log of the collision). The docstring at app.py:110-115 claims ids and digests "live in separate namespaces (h: / d:) so a sender that controls the header cannot craft a value that collides" — true across h:/d:, false within h:. Requires an authenticated sender, so impact is limited to a sender losing its own deliveries, but the fix is a one-character namespace change (e.g. `h#sha256:`).

`webhookd check` does not validate that configured secrets are decodable under the declared `scheme.secret_encoding`, so a misconfiguration that rejects 100% of production traffic passes validation. Reproduce: config with `secrets = ["zzznothex"]` and `[senders.acme.scheme] secret_encoding = "hex"`. `webhookd check --config c.toml` exits 0 and reports `secrets 1 configured` with no error or warning. At runtime every delivery to that sender gets `401 {"error": "invalid_signature"}` — `decode_secret` (src/webhookd/signatures.py:82-85) raises SignatureError, which app.py:314-316 converts to a blanket 401. The cause is at least logged server-side (`WARNING webhookd.app: ... signature error: secret is not valid hex: non-hexadecimal number found in fromhex() arg at position 0`), so it is diagnosable, but `check` is documented (README.md:361) as the thing that catches this class of error before deployment and here it does not. A single `decode_secret` call per secret in `_build_sender` would catch it at startup.

405 responses carry the permitted method in the JSON body but not in an `Allow` HTTP header, which RFC 9110 §15.5.6 requires. Observed: `curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8099/hooks/acme` returns `HTTP/1.0 405 Method Not Allowed` with headers Content-Type / Content-Length / X-Request-Id / Cache-Control only, and body `{"allow": "POST", "error": "method_not_allowed", ...}`. src/webhookd/app.py:223-228 passes `allow="POST"` as `_Rejected(**extra)`, which app.py:170 merges into the payload dict rather than into the header list. Cosmetic for webhook senders, but it will trip strict HTTP conformance checkers and proxies that key on the header.
